authorship: External trivia enthusiasts, collected by Joshi, Choi, Weld and Zettlemoyer (2017). Implementing assistant does not author or rewrite question text.
terms: Upstream repository states Apache-2.0 applies to code and data; bundled README separately limits the dataset/derived data to non-commercial research and disclaims ownership. Preserve both notices and original question-source references. Raw data, selected question/answer files and detailed answer-bearing reports stay local and ignored. This is not public/commercial rights clearance.
sampling: Ascending SHA-256 of UTF-8 cluelab-external-v1 + U+000A + QuestionId; first 1000 per upstream train/dev split form declared candidate pools. Select first eligible 50 train as development and 150 dev as local test, never upstream hidden test.
eligibility: Unchanged nonempty question <=4096 characters; Answer.Type WikipediaEntity and nonempty MatchedWikiEntityName; valid nonempty string aliases <=200 characters without pipes/control characters, plus upstream matched title; no deictic image/audio requirement. Duplicate IDs/questions/answer aliases across selected cases and exact prior ClueLab question texts excluded. Coverage and retrieval scores never determine eligibility.
corpus: Every regular .txt shard in the original 80-file coursework wikiPages directory, sorted by filename; strict existing article boundaries; byte-identical snapshots, complete articles and all valid titles including redirects/disambiguations. No question-based document selection or excerpt tailoring.
normalization: Existing Evaluation.normalize: String.trim, Locale.ROOT lowercase, collapse default Java ASCII whitespace runs to one space. No punctuation/article stripping, fuzzy matching, wrapper removal or new alias invention. Upstream aliases/value/matched entity name are projected mechanically to article-title labels and deduplicated under that normalization.
coverage: Any accepted normalized title among all indexed article titles; separately classify canonical-title, alias-only, missing. Coverage is a title-availability check, not factual support approval. Missing coverage remains in the full denominator.
queryInput: Verbatim upstream Question only; no category, answer, aliases, support, question-source URL or evaluation metadata.
comparison: Baseline first, development then local test. No ranking variants, scorer changes, stop-list change, tuning or opponent promotion in this milestone. Prior pilot numbers use different source scopes and are not comparative improvements.
failureReview: After evaluation, inspect the first three canonical-title ranking misses, first two missing-coverage cases, first alias-only case, first redirect answer and first misleading shared-term case in frozen test order when available. Report findings without changing labels or cases.
exclusions: Every candidate-pool ID has a selected/excluded disposition and reason. Entire upstream files are fingerprinted; questions outside the deterministic 1000-ID pools are accounted for by counts, not silently treated as reviewed.
